connection_maps.interpretation: A connection map is part of the constitutive factor semantics: wye and delta loads can share the same bus and graph while observing different terminal-voltage coordinates.
connection_maps.model_scope: one balanced three-phase bus with explicit phase and neutral terminals and fixed wye/delta connection maps

load_models.interpretation: The graph is fixed, but the constitutive load relation changes voltages, currents, and the decision-feasible set.
load_models.model_scope: two-bus scalar AC load models with fixed source, series impedance, and nominal demand

load_continuation.interpretation: The continuation probe records a branch-tracking and iteration-failure boundary for one scalar fixture; it is not a global voltage-collapse theorem or a ranking of load models.
load_continuation.model_scope: two-bus scalar AC continuation probe using damped fixed-point branch tracking and demand scale

ct_saturation_probe.interpretation: A declared saturation cap can change the relay decision; it is a sensitivity probe, not a CT electromagnetic model.

explicit_earth.interpretation: An explicit earth conductor and its outage/fault observations are not recoverable from a simple graph or an ideal reference alone; this is a scoped E_2 witness, not a complete protection model.
explicit_earth.model_scope: one-phase explicit-earth-conductor fixture with a finite neutral bond, maintenance outage, two fault classes, and CT-scaled protection observation

grounding_models.interpretation: Changing the grounding relation leaves simple connectivity unchanged but changes neutral voltage, return-current allocation, and grounding observations.
grounding_models.model_scope: one-phase two-conductor load with explicit neutral return and three customer-end grounding relations
